name: Azure Devops Pr Helper
description: Extenstion for VS Code to raise Azure DevOps PR without leaving the VS Code window
body:
Azure DevOps PR Helper

A VS Code extension to streamline creating Pull Requests on Azure DevOps with AI-powered title and description generation using Anthropic, Google Gemini, or OpenAI.

Features

  • Create PRs directly from VS Code - No need to switch to the browser
  • AI-Powered Suggestions - Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenAI generates PR titles and descriptions from branch, commit, and diff context
  • Work Item Linking - Link PRs to Azure DevOps work items
  • Secure Credential Storage - PAT and API keys stored using VS Code SecretStorage
  • Workspace-Aware Auto-Detection - Automatically detects the branch and repository from the active VS Code workspace folder
  • Comprehensive Settings - All configuration in one place

Installation

  1. Open VS Code and go to the Extensions view (Ctrl+Shift+X / Cmd+Shift+X).
  2. Search for Azure DevOps PR Helper and install it. (Alternatively, install from a .vsix file using the "Install from VSIX..." option in the Extensions menu).

How to Use

1. Initial Setup

Before creating your first pull request, configure your connection:

  1. Click the Azure DevOps PR icon in the VS Code Activity Bar to open the sidebar, or run the command Azure DevOps: Open Settings.
  2. Under Azure DevOps Connection, enter your Organization URL, Project Name, and a Personal Access Token (PAT). Click Save.
  3. (Optional) Under AI Provider Integration, choose Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenAI and enter the provider API key to enable AI-powered PR titles and descriptions.

2. Creating a Pull Request

Once configured, you have two ways to create pull requests:

Option A: The Sidebar (Quick Action)

  1. Open the Azure DevOps PR view in the Activity Bar.
  2. The extension automatically detects your current branch, repository, and active changes.
  3. If an AI provider is configured, click Generate Using AI to draft a context-aware title and description from your commits and diff.
  4. Click Create Pull Request.

Option B: The Full Webview (Detailed View)

  1. Run the command Azure DevOps: Create Pull Request from the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P).
  2. Select your target branch, adjust the AI-generated description, and manually link Azure DevOps Work Items if needed.
  3. Click Create to instantly open the PR on Azure DevOps.

3. AI Generation

When an AI provider is configured, the extension can analyze your git diff and local commit history to write a structured, descriptive summary of your changes.

Configuration

Open the settings panel via Command Palette: Azure DevOps: Open Settings

Azure DevOps Settings

Setting Description
Organization URL Your Azure DevOps org URL (e.g., https://dev.azure.com/your-org)
Project Project name containing your repositories
PAT Personal Access Token with Code and Work Items permissions
API Version Azure DevOps REST API version (default: 7.1)

AI Provider Settings

Setting Description
Provider Anthropic, Google Gemini, or OpenAI
API Key Provider API key stored securely in VS Code SecretStorage
Model Provider model id. Leave blank in VS Code settings to use the provider default
Max Tokens Maximum response length (default: 1024)
Temperature Creativity level 0-2 (default: 0.3)

AI Behavior Toggles

Setting Description
Enable AI Suggestions Use the selected AI provider to generate PR titles/descriptions
Generate Description Also generate description (not just title)
Auto-Accept AI Skip confirmation and use AI content directly

Privacy Settings

Setting Description
Enable Analytics Send anonymous usage data to help improve the extension

Commands

Command Description
Azure DevOps: Raise PR Create a new pull request
Azure DevOps: Copy Last PR URL Copy the last created PR URL
Azure DevOps: Clear Azure DevOps PAT Remove stored PAT
Azure DevOps: Open Settings Open the settings panel
Azure DevOps: Generate PR Title with AI Generate a title using AI

Project Structure

src/
├── extension.ts          # Entry point
├── api/
│   ├── azureDevOps.ts    # Azure DevOps API client
│   └── ai.ts             # Multi-provider AI client
├── commands/
│   ├── raisePR.ts        # PR creation command
│   ├── copyUrl.ts        # Copy URL command
│   ├── clearPAT.ts       # Clear credentials command
│   ├── generateTitle.ts  # AI title generation
│   └── index.ts          # Command exports
├── webviews/
│   ├── settingsPanel.ts  # Settings webview
│   ├── sidebarProvider.ts # Sidebar webview
│   └── index.ts          # Webview exports
├── utils/
│   ├── constants.ts      # Configuration keys and defaults
│   ├── git.ts            # Git utilities
│   ├── helpers.ts        # General utilities
│   └── services.ts       # Extension services wrapper
└── types/
    └── index.ts          # TypeScript interfaces

Security

  • Azure DevOps PAT and AI provider API keys are stored securely using VS Code's SecretStorage API
  • Credentials are never exposed in logs or configuration files
  • CSP headers protect webviews from XSS attacks

Analytics & Privacy

This extension collects anonymous usage analytics to help improve the product. We use PostHog for analytics.

What We Track

Event Description
Extension activated When the extension starts
PR created/failed Success and failure rates for PR creation
AI generation used When AI title/description generation is used
Settings changed Which settings are being configured
Connection tests Success/failure of Azure DevOps and AI provider connections

What We DON'T Track

  • No personal information - We never collect names, emails, or identifiable data
  • No code or content - We never see your PR titles, descriptions, branch names, or code
  • No repository data - We don't collect repository names or project details
  • No credentials - Your PAT and API keys are never transmitted

Privacy Controls

Analytics respects your preferences:

  1. VS Code Telemetry Setting - If you've disabled telemetry in VS Code settings, we won't collect any data
  2. Extension Setting - You can disable analytics specifically for this extension in Settings → Privacy → Enable Analytics

Anonymous User ID

We use VS Code's built-in machineId (already anonymized by VS Code) to count unique users. This ID cannot be traced back to you.

Requirements

  • VS Code 1.60.0 or higher
  • Git repository connected to Azure DevOps
  • Azure DevOps PAT with:
    • Code (Read & Write)
    • Work Items (Read & Write)
  • Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenAI API key (optional, for AI features)

License

MIT

Author

Built by Abhishek Verma

name: Claude Code Predictor
description: An AI-assisted code prediction and developer productivity tool powered by Claude, designed to anticipate code patterns, accelerate development workflows, and reduce repetitive engineering effort through intelligent context-aware suggestions and automation.
body:
Claude Code Predictor

A VS Code extension that provides AI-powered code suggestions using Anthropic's Claude models.

Features

  • Real-time code predictions and suggestions
  • Support for multiple programming languages
  • Two options for using Claude:
    1. Cloud-based Claude API
    2. Local Claude Code CLI (if installed)
  • Customizable settings for prediction behavior
  • Keyboard shortcuts for triggering predictions

Installation

  1. Install the extension from the VS Code Marketplace
  2. Configure your Claude API key or set up Claude Code CLI

Setting Up

Option 1: Using Claude API

  1. Get an API key from Anthropic
  2. In VS Code, either:
    • Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or Cmd+Shift+P on macOS) and search for "Claude Code Predictor: Set API Key"
    • When prompted automatically on first use
  3. Enter your API key when prompted

Option 2: Using Claude Code CLI (Local)

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P (or Cmd+Shift+P on macOS) and search for "Claude Code Predictor: Setup Claude Code CLI"
  2. Follow the instructions in the setup guide
  3. Once installed, the extension will automatically detect and use Claude Code CLI

Using the Extension

  • As you type, the extension will automatically suggest code completions
  • Press Alt+C to manually trigger a code suggestion
  • Code suggestions appear as standard VS Code completions

Configuration Options

  • claudeCodePredictor.apiKey: Your Claude API key (stored securely)
  • claudeCodePredictor.model: The Claude model to use for predictions
  • claudeCodePredictor.contextLines: Number of preceding lines to use for context
  • claudeCodePredictor.useClaudeCodeCLI: Whether to use local Claude Code CLI
  • claudeCodePredictor.claudeCodePath: Custom path to Claude Code binary (if not in PATH)

Security

  • Your API key is stored in VS Code's secure storage
  • When using Claude Code CLI, no API key is required as authentication is handled by the CLI
  • Code context is only sent to Claude's API or processed locally with Claude Code CLI

Troubleshooting

API Key Issues

If you're having trouble with your API key:

  1. Try setting it again with the "Claude Code Predictor: Set API Key" command
  2. Check that the API key is valid in your Anthropic account
  3. Try clearing and re-entering your API key

Claude Code CLI Issues

If Claude Code CLI isn't working:

  1. Verify installation with claude-code --version in your terminal
  2. Check that you've authenticated with claude-code auth login
  3. Restart VS Code after installing Claude Code

Privacy & Data Usage

  • Code context is sent to Claude API for processing
  • No code is stored by the extension beyond the current session
  • When using Claude Code CLI, processing happens through your local account

License

MIT

name: Design Spec Generator
description: An AI-driven design specification generator that transforms UI designs into structured development-ready specs, helping bridge the gap between designers and engineers. Built to automate design documentation, improve handoff clarity, and accelerate frontend implementation workflows.
body:
Design Spec Generator

AI-powered design specification and workflow automation tool that creates professional documentation directly in Figma. Built for the cargoes-runner design system.

Overview

Design Spec Generator automates design system workflows using AI agents and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It handles everything from component documentation to accessibility audits, design system compliance checks, and multi-platform handoffs.

Inspired by Uber's uSpec and the MCP Adoption Toolkit for design teams.

Features

Spec Generation (6 skills)

  • Anatomy: Numbered markers + attribute tables
  • API: Property documentation with types and defaults
  • Properties: Variant grid with live previews
  • Color: Design token annotations per state
  • Structure: Spacing, padding, dimension specs
  • Screen Reader: VoiceOver, TalkBack, ARIA specs

Design Workflows (5 skills)

  • Accessibility Audit: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance checking
  • Design System Audit: Detect hardcoded values and token violations
  • Ticket Validation: Compare designs against acceptance criteria
  • Multi-Tech Handoff: Generate specs for React, Angular, SwiftUI, Compose
  • Token Migration: Audit and batch migrate hardcoded values

Quick Start

Prerequisites

  • Cursor or Claude Code
  • Figma Desktop (not web version)
  • Node.js 18+
  • Figma Personal Access Token

1. Get a Figma Token

  1. Go to Figma API Settings
  2. Create a new Personal Access Token
  3. Enable scopes: File content (Read), Variables (Read), Comments (Read and write)
  4. Copy the token (starts with figd_)

2. Configure MCP

Update .mcp.json in the project root:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "figma-console": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "figma-console-mcp@latest"],
      "env": {
        "FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN": "figd_YOUR_TOKEN_HERE",
        "ENABLE_MCP_APPS": "true"
      }
    }
  }
}

3. Install Desktop Bridge Plugin

  1. Open Figma Desktop
  2. Go to Plugins → Development → Import plugin from manifest
  3. Navigate to this project and select figma-plugin/manifest.json
  4. Run the Design Spec Generator - Desktop Bridge plugin in your Figma file

Note: The plugin is included in this project at figma-plugin/. You only need to import it once.

4. Run First-Time Setup

In Cursor, open this project and run:

@firstrun

Follow the prompts to configure your template library.

Usage

Spec Generation Skills

# Generate anatomy spec with markers and tables
@create-anatomy https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
This is a Button with label, icons, loading state.

# Generate API documentation
@create-api https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Dropdown with single/multi-select, searchable, async loading.

# Generate variant exhibit
@create-properties https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456

# Generate color token annotations
@create-color https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456

# Generate dimension specs
@create-structure https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456

# Generate accessibility specs
@create-screen-reader https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Interactive button with loading and disabled states.

Design Workflow Skills

# Validate design against ticket requirements
@validate-ticket https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Acceptance Criteria:
1. User can enter email and password
2. Form shows validation errors
3. Loading state during submission

# Audit for WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
@audit-accessibility https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Focus on the login form components.

# Check design system compliance
@audit-design-system https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Audit for hardcoded colors and spacing.

# Generate multi-platform handoff
@handoff-multi-tech https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Button with primary, secondary, tertiary variants.
Generate for React and SwiftUI.

# Migrate hardcoded values to tokens
@migrate-tokens https://figma.com/design/.../node-id=123:456
Migrate all hardcoded colors to design tokens.

All Available Skills

Skill Category Description
@firstrun Setup One-time configuration wizard
@create-anatomy Spec Numbered markers + attribute table
@create-api Spec Property documentation with types
@create-properties Spec Variant grid with live previews
@create-color Spec Design token annotations
@create-structure Spec Spacing and dimension specs
@create-screen-reader Spec VoiceOver, TalkBack, ARIA specs
@validate-ticket Workflow Compare design vs acceptance criteria
@audit-accessibility Workflow WCAG 2.1 AA compliance audit
@audit-design-system Workflow Detect hardcoded values/violations
@handoff-multi-tech Workflow Multi-platform implementation specs
@migrate-tokens Workflow Batch migrate to design tokens

Project Structure

design-spec-generator/
├── .cursor/skills/              # Cursor agent skills
│   ├── firstrun/
│   ├── create-anatomy/
│   ├── create-api/
│   ├── create-properties/
│   ├── create-color/
│   ├── create-structure/
│   ├── create-screen-reader/
│   ├── validate-ticket/         # NEW
│   ├── audit-accessibility/     # NEW
│   ├── audit-design-system/     # NEW
│   ├── handoff-multi-tech/      # NEW
│   └── migrate-tokens/          # NEW
├── .claude/skills/              # Claude Code skills (mirror)
├── reference/
│   ├── accessibility/
│   │   ├── aria.md              # Web ARIA reference
│   │   ├── voiceover.md         # iOS VoiceOver reference
│   │   ├── talkback.md          # Android TalkBack reference
│   │   └── wcag-checklist.md    # WCAG 2.1 AA checklist
│   ├── component-patterns/
│   │   └── cargoes-runner.md    # Design system patterns
│   └── handoff/
│       └── platform-conventions.md  # React/Angular/Swift/Compose
├── templates/
│   ├── figma-template-guide.md  # Figma template creation guide
│   └── prompt-templates.md      # Copy-paste prompt templates
├── config/
│   └── spec-generator.config.json
├── .mcp.json                    # MCP configuration
├── CLAUDE.md                    # Claude Code instructions
└── README.md

Configuration

MCP Servers

The project uses two MCP servers:

Server Purpose
figma-console Deep canvas control, tokens, variables, components
figma-mcp-server Code Connect features, design context reading

Workflow Settings

config/spec-generator.config.json contains workflow-specific settings:

{
  "workflows": {
    "accessibility": {
      "defaultStandard": "WCAG21AA",
      "contrastThresholds": { "normalText": 4.5, "largeText": 3.0 }
    },
    "handoff": {
      "platforms": ["react", "angular", "swiftui", "compose"]
    },
    "migration": {
      "batchSize": 50,
      "dryRunFirst": true
    }
  }
}

Reference Documentation

Accessibility

  • reference/accessibility/aria.md - Web ARIA roles, states, keyboard patterns
  • reference/accessibility/voiceover.md - iOS VoiceOver traits and patterns
  • reference/accessibility/talkback.md - Android TalkBack semantics
  • reference/accessibility/wcag-checklist.md - WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria

Platform Handoff

  • reference/handoff/platform-conventions.md - Code patterns for:
    • React with Tailwind CSS
    • Angular with CSS Modules
    • SwiftUI for iOS
    • Jetpack Compose for Android

Design System

  • reference/component-patterns/cargoes-runner.md - Component APIs and tokens

Prompt Templates

See templates/prompt-templates.md for copy-paste templates:

  • Accessibility audit prompts
  • Design system audit prompts
  • Ticket validation prompts
  • Multi-platform handoff prompts
  • Token migration prompts

MCP Tools Available

When connected to Figma Console MCP:

Tool Purpose
figma_get_status Check connection status
figma_get_file_data Get full file structure
figma_get_component Extract component data
figma_get_variables Get design tokens
figma_get_styles Get color/text/effect styles
figma_execute Run Figma Plugin API code
figma_take_screenshot Capture screenshots
figma_batch_create_variables Create tokens in batch
figma_batch_update_variables Update tokens in batch

Best Practices

Session Management

  • Start fresh sessions for each skill
  • Each skill uses significant context
  • Don't chain multiple skills in one session

During Generation

  • Don't interact with Figma while generating
  • Keep Desktop Bridge plugin running
  • Wait for completion before making changes

Providing Context

  • Describe states not visible in the current frame
  • List all variants and their purposes
  • Mention edge cases and error states

Cost Management

  • Scope sessions to specific components/pages
  • Run audits before migrations
  • Use batch operations for efficiency

Troubleshooting

"MCP not connected"

  1. Ensure Figma Desktop is running (not web)
  2. Run the Desktop Bridge plugin in your Figma file
  3. Check the MCP server is configured in .mcp.json

"Template not found"

Run @firstrun to configure your template library.

"Component not found"

Verify the Figma URL contains a valid node-id parameter.

"Skills not showing in Cursor"

  1. Ensure this project folder is open in Cursor
  2. Check .cursor/skills/ contains the skill folders
  3. Restart Cursor

"Token migration failed"

  1. Check if the file is editable
  2. Verify you have edit permissions
  3. Try smaller batches

Security

  • All processing runs locally via Figma Console MCP
  • No design data sent to external APIs
  • WebSocket connection stays on localhost
  • Figma token stored locally in .mcp.json

Credits

  • Inspired by Uber's uSpec
  • Built on Figma Console MCP by Southleft
  • Workflow patterns from MCP Adoption Toolkit by Hugo França
  • Designed for cargoes-runner design system

License

MIT

name: Environment Sync
description: A lightweight developer utility for synchronizing environment configurations across projects and machines, helping teams maintain consistent .env setups with minimal friction. Built to simplify configuration management, reduce setup time, and streamline local development workflows.
body:
Environment Manager

Overview

The Environment Manager is a comprehensive tool-set for managing and tracking the current environment configuration across UI applications. It consists of:

  1. JavaScript File: A script to get the current environment and app related configurations.
  2. Node.js Application: An app to set and store the environment in a file.
  3. Chrome Extension: An extension to set the environment directly from the Chrome browser.

Components

1. JavaScript File

Purpose: Returns the current environment and app configs.

Usage:

  • Include the script at the top of your project in app.ts.
  • pass the appName to get the app relate configuration
Application appName
Web Service web-service
OMS oms
Manage manage

Code:

/**
 * LOCAL CONFIGURATION
 * [Should never be pushed]
 */
import getEnvironmentConfig from '[PATH-TO-ENVIRONMENT-SYNC]/local-config/activeConfig';
const currentConfig = getEnvironmentConfig('appName');
/**
 * Local configuration ends here
 */

2. Chrome Extension

Purpose: Allows you to set the environment directly from your Chrome browser.

Usage:

  • Load the extension into Chrome:
    • Open chrome://extensions/ in your Chrome browser.
    • Enable "Developer mode".
    • Click "Load unpacked" and select the extension directory, in this case chrome-extension.
  • Click on extensions icon and select Environment Selector.
  • A popup will appear offering a dropdown with option Development, QA, Staging for now. you can add more by yourself in the popup.html.
  • Click on Save Environment.
  • An alert will be shown saying current environment: [user selected Environment]

3. Node.js Application

Purpose: Sets the current environment and saves it to a file.

Usage:

  • Run the application using Node.js using the command npm start.
  • Application will run on port 4000.
  • As the environment is selected from the chrome-extension it will be saved to environment.json of the Node application

Steps to use

  1. import the script into your application
  2. Start the Environment Manager Node.js server
  3. Load the Chrome extension
  4. Select the environment and refresh the page

Contributing

Feel free to open issues or submit pull requests if you have suggestions or improvements!

Note

Add all your domains in host_permissions of manifest.json

"host_permissions": [
    "https://dev-runner.cargoes.com/*",
    "https://qa-runner.cargoes.com/*",
    "https://staging-runner.cargoes.com/*"
  ],

name: Figma Compliance Checker
description: An intelligent Figma auditing and compliance validation tool that helps teams enforce design system standards, accessibility rules, component consistency, and developer handoff quality. Built to automate design reviews, detect UI inconsistencies early, and improve design-to-code reliability across large-scale products.
body:
Design Compliance Checker

A tool to verify Figma designs against design guidelines like Material Design 3 or Apple Human Interface Guidelines.

Overview

This project consists of two parts:

  1. Figma Plugin - Scans your Figma designs and checks them against design guidelines
  2. Web Dashboard - Manage custom guidelines and view detailed compliance reports

Features

Figma Plugin

  • Spacing Checker - Verifies padding, margins, and gaps against your spacing grid (e.g., 4px or 8px base unit)
  • Typography Checker - Validates fonts, sizes, line heights, and weights against type scales
  • Color Checker - Ensures colors match your design palette
  • Corner Radius Checker - Validates border radius values
  • Touch Target Checker - Flags interactive elements that are too small

Web Dashboard

  • Browse and manage design guidelines
  • Visual editor to create custom guidelines
  • Import and view compliance reports
  • Export reports as HTML or PDF

Getting Started

Figma Plugin

cd figma-plugin
npm install
npm run build

Then in Figma:

  1. Go to Plugins > Development > Import plugin from manifest
  2. Select the figma-plugin/manifest.json file

Web Dashboard

cd web-dashboard
npm install
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser.

Pre-built Guidelines

The tool comes with pre-built guidelines for:

  • Material Design 3 - Google's latest design system
  • Apple Human Interface Guidelines - iOS/macOS design standards

You can also create custom guidelines through the web dashboard.

How It Works

┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│  Figma Design   │────▶│  Figma Plugin    │────▶│  Compliance     │
│                 │     │  (Scans nodes)   │     │  Report (JSON)  │
└─────────────────┘     └──────────────────┘     └────────┬────────┘
                                                          │
                        ┌──────────────────┐              │
                        │  Web Dashboard   │◀─────────────┘
                        │  (View reports)  │
                        └──────────────────┘

Guidelines Schema

Guidelines are defined as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "id": "my-design-system",
  "name": "My Design System",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "rules": {
    "spacing": {
      "baseUnit": 4,
      "allowedValues": [0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64],
      "tolerance": 1
    },
    "typography": {
      "fontFamilies": ["Inter", "Roboto"],
      "scales": {
        "heading1": { "size": 32, "lineHeight": 40, "weight": 700 },
        "body": { "size": 16, "lineHeight": 24, "weight": 400 }
      }
    },
    "colors": {
      "palette": {
        "primary": ["#6750A4", "#EADDFF"],
        "error": ["#B3261E", "#F9DEDC"]
      }
    },
    "cornerRadius": {
      "allowedValues": [0, 4, 8, 16, 9999]
    },
    "touchTargets": {
      "minimum": 48
    }
  }
}

Project Structure

design-compliance-checker/
├── figma-plugin/
│   ├── manifest.json
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.ts           # Plugin entry point
│   │   ├── scanner.ts        # Node tree scanner
│   │   ├── types.ts          # TypeScript types
│   │   ├── checkers/         # Individual rule checkers
│   │   │   ├── spacing.ts
│   │   │   ├── colors.ts
│   │   │   ├── typography.ts
│   │   │   ├── cornerRadius.ts
│   │   │   └── touchTargets.ts
│   │   ├── guidelines/       # Pre-built guidelines
│   │   │   ├── material3.ts
│   │   │   └── appleHIG.ts
│   │   └── ui/               # Plugin UI
│   │       └── index.tsx
│   └── dist/
│       ├── main.js
│       ├── ui.js
│       └── ui.html
│
└── web-dashboard/
    ├── src/
    │   ├── pages/
    │   │   ├── Guidelines.tsx
    │   │   ├── Editor.tsx
    │   │   └── Reports.tsx
    │   ├── data/
    │   │   └── presets.ts
    │   └── types.ts
    └── index.html

License

MIT

name: Figma Design Checker
description: An AI-powered Figma design auditing tool that helps developers and designers validate UI consistency, accessibility, spacing, typography, and design system compliance before development handoff. Built to streamline design reviews, reduce visual inconsistencies, and improve design-to-code quality.
body:
Figma Design Checker

A Chrome extension that compares Figma designs with your app implementation and generates Cursor-friendly fix reports.

Features

  • Tab Detection: Automatically detects Figma and app tabs
  • Figma Spec Extraction: Extracts design specs from Figma Dev Mode panel
  • App Style Extraction: Click-to-select elements and extract computed styles
  • Smart Comparison: Compares layout, typography, colors, and effects with tolerance
  • Cursor-Ready Reports: Generates markdown reports optimized for pasting into Cursor

Installation

Developer Mode (Recommended for Development)

  1. Open Chrome and navigate to chrome://extensions/
  2. Enable Developer mode (toggle in top-right corner)
  3. Click Load unpacked
  4. Select the figma-design-checker folder
  5. The extension icon should appear in your toolbar

Generate Icons (Optional)

The extension includes an SVG icon. To generate PNG icons, you can use any image editor or online tool to export the SVG at 16x16, 32x32, 48x48, and 128x128 pixels.

Usage

Step 1: Open Both Tabs

  • Open your Figma design file in one tab
  • Open your app (the implementation) in another tab

Step 2: Enable Figma Dev Mode

In Figma:

  1. Press Shift + D or click the Dev Mode toggle (bottom-right)
  2. Select the element you want to compare
  3. Ensure the properties panel is visible on the right

Step 3: Use the Extension

  1. Click the extension icon in Chrome toolbar
  2. Select your Figma tab from the dropdown
  3. Select your App tab from the dropdown
  4. Click Capture Figma Specs (the extension will switch to Figma and extract specs)
  5. Click Select App Element (the extension will switch to your app)
  6. Click on the corresponding element in your app (it will highlight on hover)
  7. Click Compare Designs
  8. View the results and click Copy Report to Clipboard
  9. Paste into Cursor chat for automated fixes

Manual Input (Fallback)

If automatic extraction doesn't work:

  1. Expand the "Manual Input" section
  2. Paste Figma specs as JSON:
    {"padding": "16px", "fontSize": "14px", "color": "#333333"}
  3. Paste app styles as JSON:
    {"padding": "12px", "fontSize": "14px", "color": "#666666"}
  4. Click Compare Manual Input

Example Output

## Design Discrepancies Found

**Element**: <button> .primary-btn "Submit"
**Date**: 2024-01-15
**Total Issues**: 2

---

### Layout Issues

**1. Padding** [HIGH]
- **Expected** (Figma): `16px 24px`
- **Actual** (App): `12px 16px`
- **Fix**: Update padding to 16px 24px

### Typography Issues

**2. Font Weight** [MEDIUM]
- **Expected** (Figma): `600`
- **Actual** (App): `400`
- **Fix**: Update font-weight to 600

---

### Quick CSS Fix

```css
.element {
  padding: 16px 24px;
  font-weight: 600;
}

Cursor Fix Prompt

Copy and paste this into Cursor to fix the issues:

Fix the following design discrepancies for the <button> .primary-btn "Submit":

- Padding: change from `12px 16px` to `16px 24px`
- Font Weight: change from `400` to `600`

Please update the styles to match the Figma design specifications.


## Troubleshooting

### "No Figma tabs found"
- Make sure you have a Figma file open in a browser tab
- The URL should contain `figma.com`

### "Could not find design specs"
- Enable Dev Mode in Figma (Shift + D)
- Select an element in Figma
- Make sure the properties panel is visible
- Try the Manual Input fallback

### "No element selected"
- Click the "Select App Element" button first
- Click on an element in your app
- Press Escape to cancel selection

### Extension not working on internal URLs
- The extension has `<all_urls>` permission
- If blocked, check your company's Chrome extension policies

## Technical Details

### Permissions Used
- `activeTab`: Access the current tab
- `tabs`: Query and switch between tabs
- `scripting`: Inject content scripts
- `storage`: Save preferences (future feature)

### How Figma Extraction Works
The extension attempts to:
1. Find the Dev Mode panel in Figma's DOM
2. Extract text content containing CSS-like properties
3. Parse values using regex patterns

**Note**: Figma's DOM structure may change. If extraction fails, use Manual Input.

### How App Extraction Works
1. Injects a selector script that highlights elements on hover
2. On click, stores the selected element
3. Uses `window.getComputedStyle()` to extract all CSS properties

## Limitations

- Figma extraction depends on Dev Mode panel being visible
- Figma's DOM structure may change, breaking automatic extraction
- Complex nested elements may require manual selector refinement
- Color comparison has a 5-point RGB tolerance

## Contributing

Feel free to improve the Figma extraction selectors or add new features!

name: Formflow Ai Assistant
description: An AI-powered workflow and form automation assistant designed to streamline form handling, validation, and intelligent user interactions. Built to reduce manual effort, improve workflow efficiency, and enable smarter form-driven experiences through conversational AI and automation capabilities.
body:
formflow-ai-assistant

A React chatbot widget for form-driven applications. It converts natural language into structured actions that can fill react-hook-form fields, navigate tabs, and add or update table rows.

What This Package Owns

  • Chat UI: AIAssistantWidget, ChatPanel, message rendering.
  • AI orchestration: prompt building, Gemini/OpenAI request handling, response parsing.
  • Action execution: field updates, tab navigation, table handlers.
  • UI-library adapters: DOM behavior for controls that cannot be updated safely with direct form state writes, such as async dropdowns.

App/domain knowledge stays outside the package in an AIAssistantConfig.

Installation

npm install formflow-ai-assistant

Quick Start

1. Create App Config

import type { AIAssistantConfig } from 'formflow-ai-assistant';

export const aiConfig: AIAssistantConfig = {
  appType: 'shipment',
  appDescription: 'Freight shipment management for ocean and air cargo',
  fields: {
    transportMode: {
      formPath: 'transportMode',
      label: 'Transport Mode',
      type: 'dropdown',
      options: [
        { value: 'SEA', aliases: ['sea', 'ocean'] },
        { value: 'AIR', aliases: ['air', 'flight'] },
      ],
    },
    client: {
      formPath: 'client',
      label: 'Client',
      type: 'async-dropdown',
      description: 'Customer/client for this shipment',
    },
  },
  tabs: {
    main: [
      { id: 'shipmentDetails', label: 'Shipment Details', aliases: ['details'] },
      { id: 'cargo', label: 'Cargo', aliases: ['cargo', 'containers'] },
    ],
  },
};

2. Mount Provider and Widget

import { FormProvider, useForm } from 'react-hook-form';
import {
  AIAssistantWidget,
  AIAssistantProvider,
  defaultUIAdapter,
} from 'formflow-ai-assistant';
import { aiConfig } from './ai-assistant/config';

function ShipmentForm() {
  const formMethods = useForm();
  const [currentTab, setCurrentTab] = useState('shipmentDetails');

  return (
    <AIAssistantProvider
      config={aiConfig}
      formMethods={formMethods}
      tabNavigator={{
        currentTab,
        setTab: setCurrentTab,
      }}
      uiAdapter={defaultUIAdapter}
      geminiApiKey={process.env.REACT_APP_GEMINI_API_KEY}
      provider="gemini"
      model="gemini-flash-latest"
    >
      <FormProvider {...formMethods}>{/* app */}</FormProvider>
      <AIAssistantWidget position="bottom-right" />
    </AIAssistantProvider>
  );
}

UI-Library Adapters

The assistant is app-config driven, but some UI controls need real DOM interaction. Async dropdowns are the main case: direct setValue can miss option metadata or side effects, so the assistant opens the dropdown, searches, waits for API results, and selects a result.

UI-library-specific behavior lives under:

src/ui-libs/<ui-library>/

Current built-in adapter:

import { defaultUIAdapter } from 'formflow-ai-assistant';

Adapter Interface

interface UIAdapterConfig {
  asyncDropdown?: {
    getTrigger: (field: FieldConfig, formPath: string) => HTMLElement | null;
    getPopover: () => HTMLElement | null;
    getSearchInput: (popover: HTMLElement) => HTMLInputElement | null;
    getOptions: (popover: HTMLElement) => HTMLElement[];
    openWaitMs?: number;
    searchWaitMs?: number;
    afterSelectWaitMs?: number;
  };
}

The default adapter uses common accessible DOM selectors:

  • trigger: document.getElementById(formPath)
  • popover: latest [role="listbox"]
  • search input: first input inside popover
  • options: [role="option"]
  • waits: 2000ms, 2000ms, 100ms

Async dropdown action behavior:

  1. Open dropdown.
  2. Wait for initial async options.
  3. Type the requested value in the search input.
  4. Wait for searched API results.
  5. Select the first returned option.

To add another UI library, create a folder such as src/ui-libs/mui/, implement the same adapter interface, export it from src/ui-libs/index.ts, then pass it as uiAdapter from the host app.

Provider Props

interface AIAssistantProviderProps {
  config: AIAssistantConfig;
  formMethods: UseFormReturn<Record<string, unknown>>;
  tabNavigator: TabNavigator;
  tableHandlers?: Record<string, TableHandler>;
  uiAdapter?: UIAdapterConfig;
  openAIApiKey?: string;
  geminiApiKey?: string;
  claudeApiKey?: string; // deprecated alias
  provider?: 'openai' | 'gemini';
  model?: string;
  additionalSystemPrompt?: string;
  onActionExecuted?: (action: AIAction, success: boolean) => void;
  onError?: (error: Error) => void;
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

Tables

Use react-hook-form field-array handlers for table actions:

const { append, update } = useFieldArray({
  control: formMethods.control,
  name: 'containersList',
});

<AIAssistantProvider
  tableHandlers={{
    containers: { append, update },
  }}
  // ...
/>

Using Another Model or Training a Future Model

There are two different paths: using another hosted model, or training/fine-tuning a model to produce this app's action JSON more reliably.

Use Another Hosted Model

  1. Add provider support in the AI request hook (src/hooks/useOpenAIAPI.ts, or split it into provider-specific clients later).
  2. Keep the output contract unchanged: the model must return JSON with:
    {
  "message": "Human-readable response",
  "actions": []
}
  3. Add a provider name to the provider union type.
  4. Add provider-specific API key prop if needed, for example anthropicApiKey or localModelUrl.
  5. Map the provider response text into parseAIResponse.
  6. Build and test with the same app config and examples.

Fine-Tune or Train a Model for This App

  1. Keep the action schema stable. The important training target is AIResponse and AIAction, not the UI.
  2. Collect examples from real usage:
    • user request
    • relevant current form context
    • expected message
    • expected actions
  3. Store examples in the same shape as ConversationExample where possible.
  4. Include negative examples where the model should return CLARIFY instead of guessing.
  5. Train/fine-tune the model to output only valid JSON matching the action schema.
  6. Validate every model response with parseAIResponse before executing actions.
  7. Keep UI library logic out of training data. The model should decide what action to perform; the adapter decides how the UI executes it.
  8. Add regression prompts for core flows: static dropdowns, async dropdowns, tab navigation, table row creation, and ambiguous requests.

Recommended starting point: do not fine-tune immediately. First improve examples in the app config and add provider support. Fine-tune only after you have enough failed prompts or repeated workflows to justify it.

Security

Browser env keys such as REACT_APP_GEMINI_API_KEY are exposed to users. This is acceptable for local testing only. For production, route model calls through a backend proxy and keep provider keys server-side.

Troubleshooting

  • If static fields do not update, verify formPath matches react-hook-form state.
  • If async dropdowns do not work, verify the correct uiAdapter is passed.
  • If async dropdown opens but does not select, inspect the UI library's trigger, popover, search input, and option selectors.
  • If the model returns bad JSON, add examples or tighten additionalSystemPrompt.
  • If actions are valid but fail, check onActionExecuted and browser console warnings.

Validation

import { validateConfig, formatValidationErrors } from 'formflow-ai-assistant';

const errors = validateConfig(aiConfig);
if (errors.length > 0) {
  console.error(formatValidationErrors(errors));
}

License

MIT

name: Lighthouse Agent
description: A lightweight headless AI agent framework built for autonomous workflows, browser automation, and intelligent task execution. Designed to be modular, extensible, and developer-friendly, Lighthouse Agent focuses on real-world automation with minimal setup and maximum control.
body:
Lighthouse Audit Agent

A fully local Lighthouse performance auditing tool with a modern dashboard. Run audits on any URL, track scores over time, and get actionable suggestions.

Features

  • Module Organization: Group URLs into modules (e.g., "E-Commerce", "Marketing")
  • Lighthouse Audits: Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO, PWA scores
  • Authentication Support: Add login credentials for pages behind auth
  • Screenshots: Automatic full-page screenshots of each audit
  • Suggestions: Actionable improvement recommendations with estimated savings
  • Score History: Track score trends over time with charts

Quick Start

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Start the app (runs both server and dashboard)
npm run dev

Open http://localhost:5173 in your browser.

Architecture

┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│    Dashboard    │────▶│   Express API    │────▶│     SQLite      │
│   (React/Vite)  │     │   + Lighthouse   │     │   (data.db)     │
│   :5173         │     │   :4001          │     │                 │
└─────────────────┘     └──────────────────┘     └─────────────────┘

Project Structure

lighthouse-agent/
├── server/               # Backend API
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── index.ts      # Express server (port 4001)
│   │   ├── db.ts         # SQLite database
│   │   └── lighthouse.ts # Audit runner with auth support
│   ├── data.db           # SQLite database (auto-created)
│   └── screenshots/      # Captured screenshots
├── dashboard/            # Frontend
│   └── src/
│       ├── App.tsx
│       ├── components/   # React components
│       └── lib/api.ts    # API client
└── package.json

Usage

1. Create a Module

Click "Modules" tab → Enter module name → "Create Module"

2. Add URLs

Expand a module → "Add URL to this module" → Enter URL

3. Add Authentication (Optional)

For pages requiring login:

  • Click the ⚙️ icon next to a URL
  • Enter login credentials
  • The agent will authenticate before running audits

4. Run Audits

Click "Run Audit" button → Results appear automatically

API Endpoints

Method Endpoint Description
GET /api/modules List all modules
POST /api/modules Create a module
GET /api/urls List all URLs
POST /api/urls Add a URL
POST /api/audit/run Trigger audit
GET /api/audits List audit results

Database

SQLite database stored at server/data.db with tables:

  • modules - URL groups
  • urls - URLs with optional auth credentials
  • audits - Lighthouse results
  • suggestions - Improvement recommendations

Tech Stack

  • Frontend: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts
  • Backend: Node.js, Express, TypeScript
  • Database: SQLite (better-sqlite3)
  • Auditing: Lighthouse, Puppeteer

MIT

body:
Voice AR Object Placer

A WebXR augmented reality app that lets you place 3D objects in the real world using voice commands. Point your camera at a surface, tap the mic, and say "red cube" or "blue sphere" to place objects that persist as you move around.

Features

  • Surface Detection - Automatically detects flat surfaces (tables, floors, walls)
  • Voice Commands - Place objects by speaking color + shape combinations
  • Persistent Objects - Placed objects stay anchored in world space
  • Real-time Feedback - Visual reticle shows where objects will be placed

Supported Voice Commands

Speak a combination of color + shape:

Colors Shapes
red cube
blue sphere
green cylinder
yellow cone
orange
purple
white
black
pink
cyan

Examples:

  • "red cube"
  • "blue sphere"
  • "green cylinder"
  • "yellow cone"

Requirements

Device Requirements

  • Android phone with ARCore support (most phones from 2018+)
  • Chrome browser version 81 or later
  • Google Play Services for AR installed

Network Requirements

  • Must be served over HTTPS (or localhost for development)
  • Same WiFi network for local development testing

Not Supported

  • iOS Safari (Apple has not implemented WebXR AR)
  • Desktop browsers
  • Non-Chrome mobile browsers

Getting Started

Installation

npm install

Development

npm start

This starts a development server with HTTPS enabled at:

  • Local: https://localhost:8084/
  • Network: https://<your-ip>:8084/

Production Build

npm run build

Output is generated in the dist/ folder.

Testing on Android

  1. Start the dev server on your computer:

    npm start

  2. Get the network URL from the terminal output (e.g., https://192.168.x.x:8084/)

  3. On your Android phone:

    • Open Chrome browser
    • Navigate to the HTTPS URL
    • Accept the security warning (tap "Advanced" → "Proceed")
    • Allow camera and microphone permissions
    • Tap "Start AR"

  4. Using the app:

    • Point camera at a flat surface
    • Wait for the green reticle to appear
    • Tap the mic button
    • Say a command like "red cube"
    • The object appears on the surface!

Tech Stack

  • Three.js (r152) - 3D rendering
  • WebXR Device API - AR session and hit-testing
  • Web Speech API - Voice recognition
  • Webpack 5 - Bundling and dev server

Project Structure

web-xr/
├── src/
│   ├── index.html    # Main HTML with UI overlay
│   ├── index.js      # App logic (WebXR, speech, 3D)
│   └── style.css     # UI styling
├── webpack.config.js # Build configuration
└── package.json      # Dependencies

Architecture

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    User Input                           │
│  ┌─────────────┐                    ┌──────────────┐   │
│  │  Mic Button │                    │ Camera Feed  │   │
│  └──────┬──────┘                    └──────┬───────┘   │
│         │                                  │           │
│         ▼                                  ▼           │
│  ┌─────────────┐                    ┌──────────────┐   │
│  │ Web Speech  │                    │   WebXR      │   │
│  │    API      │                    │  Hit Test    │   │
│  └──────┬──────┘                    └──────┬───────┘   │
│         │                                  │           │
│         ▼                                  ▼           │
│  ┌─────────────┐                    ┌──────────────┐   │
│  │  Command    │                    │   Reticle    │   │
│  │   Parser    │                    │  Placement   │   │
│  └──────┬──────┘                    └──────────────┘   │
│         │                                              │
│         ▼                                              │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │              Three.js Scene                      │   │
│  │         (3D objects + AR overlay)                │   │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Troubleshooting

Issue Solution
"WebXR API not available" Use Chrome browser on Android
"Immersive AR not supported" Install Google Play Services for AR from Play Store
"Page must be loaded over HTTPS" Use the https:// URL, not http://
Security certificate warning Tap "Advanced" → "Proceed" (safe for local dev)
No reticle appearing Point camera at a well-lit flat surface
Voice not recognized Speak clearly, try "red cube" or "blue sphere"
iOS not working WebXR AR is not supported on iOS Safari
